caption:
Thought I’d share this on Instagram as well.

We are called by Jesus to be fruitful, and fellowship is one of the key concepts of obeying this command. In 1 John 1:1-4 we are given a blueprint to attain the Joy of the Lord & that blueprint is two-fold. We are called to first have fellowship with Jesus and then called to have fellowship with one another! As Christians we sometimes use our sanctification as a gateway to complete isolation. Yes we are set apart, but only from the things and people of this world that are not of God! We are set apart from the world to then walk in our God given purpose WITH our brothers and sisters in the Body of Christ! 

I want to use this post as an opportunity for all of us Children of God to find COMMUNITY. No, everyone is not called to be our closest friends, but we are called to fellowship as believers! So, whether it’s an online community you join or create, or a bible study you start to attend, or a faith call you begin to have with your friends, it doesn’t matter as long as you are fulfilling the will of God! I am here to merely encourage everyone to refrain from complete isolation if that is not truly the season God has you in! I love you all, God bless, and I can’t wait to continue fellowshipping with you!❤️🙏🏾

caption:
Just a kid from Chicago who never  thought I’d make it this far. From facing homelessness in high school… to losing my older brother… to giving my life to Christ… to meeting the love of my life and getting married at 21 — every step has shaped me.

 I’m breaking generational curses! I’ll be the first in my family to graduate college with a B.S. in Business Administration – Finance. 🎓

As a Black man who comes from nothing, I want my story to be proof: It’s possible. You can rise. You can break the chains that tried to hold you or your family back.

“Trust in the LORD with all your heart and lean not on your own understanding; in all your ways submit to him, and he will make your paths straight” Proverbs 3:5-6

This is my farewell… and my beginning. #explore #blackexcllence

athlete.name: Jason Henderson
athlete.bio: A relentless force on the field, this linebacker combines tactical acumen with fierce determination. Hailing from a storied football lineage, he embodies grit, leadership, and an unyielding passion for the game.

caption: Since the 5th grade football had become everything to me. It got me through life to this point. It gave me a reason to wake up each day and give it my all. November 2023 I suffered a serious injury. I tore my ACL, MCL, MPFL and meniscus. I knew it was going to be a long road of recovery. Almost two years now I have been trying to get to a point to where I can return to the football field and confidently give my all as I always do when I’m on that field. Through this process, I have tested my mental and physical strength to the max. I have done everything in my power to be as physically and mentally prepared to give it my all one last time. Unfortunately, I haven’t been able to get to the point to where I can maintain playing at a competitive level again. I have decided I am going to step away from being a football player. For the betterment of myself and future. Football has given me everything. Anyone who knows me understands I dedicated my life to football. The passion I have for football and love for the game are two things hopefully no once can question about me. I’m forever grateful for what football has given me. Football gave me a chance. Football taught me lessons. Football gave me a second family. Football will forever hold a huge part of me. I’m blessed and grateful for my career. I have given my all every single opportunity I got. I took advantage of each and every opportunity given to me. I was blessed enough to accomplish things that I couldn’t have ever dreamed of as a football player and I feel as if I have done all I could and given everything I possibly could to the sport of football. Football will forever be a part of me. I’m forever thankful.

Jared Turner who was a starting defenseman for national powerhouse Gonzaga (D.C.), is now in his 2nd season playing basketball at Northeastern. 

The Silver Spring, MD native started playing lacrosse in 1st grade and started for the Eagles lacrosse team among many DI lacrosse commits. 

The 6’8” G/F is currently averaging 7.8 PPG for the Huskies and had 19 points against GSU in November. 

In an Inside Lacrosse article from 2022 he stated “I’m definitely bringing my lacrosse sticks to Northeastern. If [the basketball coaches] would let me, I’d strongly consider playing club. I think it would be pretty fun.”

caption: The VVS program will be held in my heart forever. We all left finals last year thinking and saying we got this next year. Then next year didn’t happen. Although I would love to have won sectionals this year. Its been one hell of a ride. 7-0 and two block records later. We did it. I am so grateful to have not just been able to become friends with these girls but a family too. I will cherish these memories forever. This team has made me who I am today, improving my skills on and off the court. Success doesn’t come from those who are scared to fail and we failed a whole ton. But we also won a sh** ton too. Thank you ladies for having my back I wish it would never end. If I learned anything this year. Its we don’t always have that “oh ill do it next season.”Grab it while you can and never defer that moment. Take that opportunity now. Although this journey is over Im so excited to continue my career at Old Dominion University! I wish you all the best in your future and good luck to my younger kiddos. Love y’all. Deuces ✌🏼😢❤️🏐
